pure-announcement.rationale: Although it is Google Cloud's launch post for OKF v0.1, the thing launched is an explicitly vendor-neutral open format whose design ideas (format-not-platform, producer/consumer independence) transfer beyond any Google product.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concept llm-maintained-wiki covers the write-time distillation pattern OKF builds on but not OKF's distinct idea — a standardized interoperability format so bundles from different producers are consumable by different agents without translation.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The spec, reference implementations and sample bundles are published on GitHub, so every claim about the format is checkable.

durability.rationale: This is a just-published v0.1 spec of single-vendor origin with adoption that is entirely aspirational ('we expect the ecosystem to grow') — the same shape as the llms.txt weak exemplar: a proposed convention with no standards-body backing and no committed external consumers yet.

actionability.rationale: It advocates adopting a format and points the reader to the spec, repo and reference agent, but the note itself withholds the actionable specifics (field definitions, conformance criteria) and mostly says 'read the spec, write a producer, try our implementation'.

atomicity.rationale: It carries one coherent idea — a portable directory-of-markdown-plus-YAML format for agent knowledge — with the three design principles hanging off it as support, statable in a single paragraph.
